title: Bounded Input Rewind
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes over Boolean symbols, with states $q_s,q_c$, and a possible destination state $d$ (which may be absent). Suppose every transition from $q_s$ moves the input head left and enters $q_c$, without changing work tapes or output. Suppose every transition from $q_c$ moves left and remains in $q_c$ when it reads a Boolean symbol, and moves right and enters $d$ when it reads a blank; these transitions also leave work tapes and output unchanged. From any configuration $c$ whose state is $q_s$, there is a time $r\le p+2$, where $p$ is the current input-head position, such that after $r$ steps the configuration agrees with $c$ in every field except that its state is $d$ and its input head is at position one.
hypotheses_covered: A machine with $k$ work tapes over Boolean symbols
States $q_s$ and $q_c$, and an optional destination state $d$
The stated transition rule from $q_s$ for every input and work-tape reading
The stated transition rule from $q_c$ for every input and work-tape reading
replaced:
Consider a machine with a start state whose transition unconditionally steps the
input head left into a scanning state, and a scanning state that keeps stepping
left over input symbols and exits right into a destination state at the left
blank. Then from any configuration in the start state there is a number of steps,
at most the current input position plus $2$, after which the configuration equals
the original one with control transferred to the destination state and the input
head at cell one.
